experiment_Name: OpenRouter model price-performance sweep: CODE-ACCORD full document (v17)
experiment_Description: One v17 pipeline run per case/model on the CODE-ACCORD full-PDF-text dataset. The eight-model OpenRouter roster keeps GPT-5.4 as the prior-result anchor; GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol as current OpenAI comparisons; Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon as updated frontier comparisons; Qwen 3.6 Plus and MiniMax M3.1 Flash as value candidates; and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 as a long-context candidate. This 17 October 2026 model snapshot accepts text and images, but these configurations supply text-only documents. OpenRouter lists a 1.0M-token context; the OpenInference endpoint lists $0.02/M input and $1/M output, while other providers list different rates. Its pinned OpenRouter model ID is deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017. These provider descriptions and prices motivate candidate selection but do not establish expected extraction quality. Provider performance claims are hypotheses, not results. Compare exact-match rates separately by dataset and report scored/unscored outputs, tokens, pipeline time, and dated API-equivalent cost. One pipeline run per case/model is descriptive screening, not a stable model ranking; v17 may make a second LLM call during context expansion. The full-PDF dataset has 292 records; this configuration filters to the 290 filenames in the expanded-passage reference set. CODE-ACCORD questions guide chunk retrieval and are appended to the extraction prompt. The pipeline ranks full-document text and selects chunks, so the model's maximum context does not imply that every full PDF is sent verbatim in one call.
